registered: 2026-11-07, agent (Milestone 4 of plans/evidence-layer.md, Eric's #22 decision: $5 cap)
approval: No paid call (judge or extractor) runs until Eric approves the SHA-256 of this exact file. A change to any bound file requires a new manifest and a new approval.
question: Does adding the OpenRouter cloudflare/clairic extractor line to chat_evidence (arm C) give located, correct answers often enough, and mislead rarely enough, to turn --optchat-extract on by default?

cases.provenance: Synthetic chats authored by the seeded generator; no real chat text, no traces. Unicode cases put emoji and accented letters before the answer, so they double as the live span-unit probe.

arms.A: chat_recall: production recall() with shipped defaults (recall-min 0.5, k 1, seeds 8), host judge role; report only, not in the adoption rule.
arms.C: B plus the production openRouterExtractor (cloudflare/clairic, return_state_text), shown below p_null 0.5 (the shipped --optchat-extract-null default).

run.preflight: --mode oracle (no provider call) must score C 1.0 grounded and abstain success with 0 errors before the live run.
run.budget: $2 ceiling across both paid arms (A $1, C $1), inside Eric's $5 cap; concurrency can overshoot a cap by up to 4 calls.
run.reruns: Only rows in errors.jsonl may be rerun, once.

metrics: span probe: echo matches and span text equals value

adoption.rule: Turn --optchat-extract on by default only if all hold for C: misleading <= 0.05; groundedSuccess >= 0.70; every span-bearing answer has echo === state, and span text equals value in >= 0.95 of them; cost known on every row and mean <= $0.0005 per row; latency p90 <= 5000 ms. Otherwise keep C off by default (opt-in flag stays) and record the rejection.
adoption.inconclusive: More than 5% error rows, unknown cost on any C row, or a cap exhausted before every row ran: inconclusive, C stays off.
adoption.limits: Synthetic chats with a deterministic head summariser measure the extractor on known passages, not real-summary navigation; A's numbers are context, not a verdict on chat_recall.
